output.review_comment: Most of this PR is reasonable: splitting words longer than `width` into chunks, returning [] for empty or whitespace-only input, and not adding an empty final line. However, changing the fit check from `<=` to `<` is not right. Lines built by joining words must now be strictly shorter than `width`, but a single split chunk can be exactly `width` long, so the code applies two different length limits. For example, `wrap_text("ab cd", 5)` should return ["ab cd"] (5 chars, which is within width) but now returns ["ab", "cd"]. The PR description even says this difference is intended. A wrap function normally allows lines up to and including `width`, and the teammate said the docstring is the source of truth. This looks like a change made to get one test to pass rather than a real fix. Please restore `<=`, find which test actually failed and why (probably something in how chunks or the final line are handled), and fix that against the docstring.
